End-to-end tutorials

Ship real projects, end to end

The other Academy tracks teach concepts. This one walks you through complete BrewSLM projects — from picking a dataset to packaging a trained model and getting its serve commands. Each tutorial is one specific use case: support FAQ, SQL injection classifier, invoice extraction, customer ticket triage, internal knowledge-base QA, code review, PII span tagging, and two on domain packs (legal contracts, finance). Same workflow shape, different recipe per use case. New to BrewSLM? Start with Tutorial 0 — it sets you up (backend, frontend, and the Redis + Celery worker that every training step needs) and tours the UI in about 20 minutes so the rest of the tutorials make sense.

Start with Tutorial 0 → All tracks
  1. 0. Set up BrewSLM and your first project

    Clone the repo, start the backend on port 8000, start Redis and the Celery worker that runs training, start the frontend on port 5173, log in as the bootstrap admin user, create an empty project, tour the six workspace destinations (Overview, Data, Train, Results, Ship, Settings) and the notification bell, then smoke-test one training run on a starter demo so a missing Redis or worker shows up now. The prerequisite for every other tutorial. Includes troubleshooting for the most common first-time issues (port conflicts, pip install failures, an empty project list after sign-in, a training run that never makes progress).

    Recipe: n/a · Time: ~20 min · Difficulty: beginner

  2. 1. Build a support FAQ assistant with the rag-protocol recipe

    End-to-end: pick a dataset of FAQ triples (context, question, answer with citation), build a 60-row answer key (gold set), generate refusal / citation / format drills via the rag-protocol playbooks, train, pick the rag-protocol discipline rule set (citation, hallucination and refusal rates) and score against it, then export the model and read its serve plan. Retrieval at serving time stays your job, or the BrewSLM gateway's. Domain-agnostic — the same recipe works for ecom FAQ, legal QA, internal IT support, healthcare KBs.

    Recipe: rag-protocol · Time: ~2h · Difficulty: intermediate

  3. 2. SQL injection classifier (security)

    A binary classifier that flags injection-shaped queries inline before your DB layer, in milliseconds. Covers the classification recipe, the hard-negatives playbook (the make-or-break drill for security classifiers), per-class rules (benign recall is the one that caps false blocks), an adversarial held-out set for novel-pattern generalisation, and the shadow-mode → tee-mode → inline-blocking deployment progression. Public datasets (OWASP, Kaggle) get you started; your own application logs supply the hard negatives.

    Recipe: classification · Time: ~2.5h · Difficulty: intermediate

  4. 3. Invoice field extraction (structured)

    A structured-extraction model that pulls vendor, total, line items, and dates out of free-form invoice text. Starts with the choice between json-extraction (one typed value per field, the default for ERP posting) and span-extraction (offsets and line items), then walks the span-extraction recipe with span-set scoring, answer-key construction via the span-tagging workbench, LLM-assisted promotion from existing AP records, a template-disjoint split (no invoice template in both train and test), and per-entity precision floors (the "total" gate sits tighter than "line items"). Public starting points, with their licences: FUNSD, CORD, SROIE.

    Recipe: json-extraction or span-extraction · Time: ~2.5h · Difficulty: intermediate

  5. 4. Customer ticket triage (multi-class)

    Route incoming tickets to the right team automatically. Covers multi-class classification, class-imbalance diagnosis via the Shannon entropy signal in the Quality and safety panel (Data → Prepare → Details), the Balance class distribution playbook as the headline drill, per-class F1 floors (the gate that catches a "starving" rare class), and a confidence-thresholded routing pattern: auto-route on high confidence, shadow-route on mid, queue on low.

    Recipe: classification · Time: ~2.5h · Difficulty: intermediate

  6. 5. Internal knowledge-base QA (qa-sft path)

    The qa-sft counterpart to Tutorial 1's rag-protocol. When to pick memorisation over retrieval: small (<100 facts), stable corpora, offline-operation requirements, no citation discipline needed. Covers the decision matrix vs rag-protocol, the two qa-sft playbooks (paraphrase + cluster-targeted — note hard-negatives and class-balance-fill are NOT shipped for this recipe), and what to do when the post-eval decision engine recommends a reroute-to-RAG (the one-click sibling-project clone).

    Recipe: qa-sft · Time: ~2h · Difficulty: intermediate

  7. 6. Code review nitpicker

    Train a model to comment on code diffs the way your senior engineers do. Covers the code-review recipe, LLM-judge as the primary eval gate (since "right answer" is rarely exact-match for reviews), the by-author / by-repo split to prevent stylistic leakage, the hard-negatives playbook for "LGTM that should have flagged a bug" examples, and a comment-only rollout before the model can block a merge. Answer-key rows can be typed in by hand (input + expected output, multi-line) or bulk-imported. Public starting points: CodeReviewer, CodeSearchNet, your own PR archive.

    Recipe: code-review · Time: ~2.5h · Difficulty: intermediate

  8. 7. PII span tagging (safety)

    Highlight emails / phone numbers / addresses / SSNs / credit cards in free-form text. Sibling tutorial to #3 (same span-extraction recipe, different annotation pattern: closed-set extraction vs open-set tagging), trained as token classification (an encoder tagger with exact offsets, tunable thresholds and Try redaction), with the causal-LM path as the alternative. Covers per-entity recall floors you set as policy (for example SSN ≥ 0.98, names ≥ 0.85), Faker-synthesized training data (never train on real PII), and the explicit-review-before-redaction pattern (audit log required; no auto-redact without keeping the original).

    Recipe: span-extraction (token classification) · Time: ~2.5h · Difficulty: intermediate

  9. 8. Legal contracts via a custom domain pack

    The headline tutorial for the domain-pack layer. The only built-in domain pack is the general one (a Legal domain preset and a legal eval pack exist, but no legal pack), so you build one. Covers what a domain pack IS (a typed configuration overlay on top of a recipe), the Domain Packs panel (Settings → Tools), the cleaning + eval-threshold + glossary fields you can override, how packs are assigned per project (resolved live, so duplicate before editing), AND the current gap honestly documented: refusals are detected by a fixed phrase list, so keep the standard refusal phrase in your legal refusals or the refusal metric can't see them.

    Recipe: rag-protocol + custom legal pack · Time: ~3h · Difficulty: intermediate-advanced

  10. 9. Building domain packs — the deep reference (finance / AP example)

    The canonical deep-dive on pack construction. T8 used legal as a quick walkthrough; this tutorial is ~70% pack methodology and ~30% finance worked example. Covers pack anatomy field-by-field (sourced from domain_pack_service.py), the cleaning / evaluator / glossary overlays, currency normalisation per region, per-entity precision priorities tied to SOX key controls, versioning and sharing packs as zip files, applying one pack to invoice + PO + statement projects, and the anti-patterns that wreck packs in the long run. It also documents what the platform leaves to your team: default-normalizer is a pass-through, safe-cleanup-normalizer (★ in the picker) is the recommended swap-in among 8 other built-in normalizers such as whitespace-collapse-normalizer and currency-canonical-normalizer, and per-entity gating lives in the eval pack, not the domain pack.

    Recipe: span-extraction + custom finance pack · Time: ~3.5h · Difficulty: advanced

What's covered in every tutorial

Each tutorial walks the same 15 stages so once you've done one, the rest are a different shape of the same workflow:

  1. What you'll build (concrete deliverable)
  2. Why this approach (cost / latency / scope framing)
  3. Dataset selection (public sources + your own)
  4. Ingestion + adapter mapping
  5. Cleanup + PII review
  6. Recipe pick (decision tree)
  7. Domain pack (when applicable)
  8. Answer key (gold set) — manual + LLM-assisted, under Data → Labels
  9. Train / val / test split
  10. Synthetic data drills (recipe-specific playbooks)
  11. Review queue for generated rows (imported rows skip it and train directly)
  12. Training configuration
  13. Trainability forecast read
  14. Evaluation against the project's pass/fail rules (Results → Verdict; the recipe's rules apply only after Use scaffold, or after you pick a rule set in the Project rule set picker, both on Results → Failures)
  15. Shipping (smoke-test on Results → Try it, export on Ship → Package, serve commands from the export's Serve Plan)
